facts.statement: Ofcom published the 2026 planned network deployments report on 13 May 2026.
The report examines planned very-high-capacity network deployment through the end of 2028.
The report includes fixed-wireless-access network extension and upgrade plans.
Operator plans were stated as of January 2026 and cover the following three years.
Plans include privately funded and publicly supported deployments.
The report excludes separate public-authority rollout aspirations not represented in operator plans.
The planned report supplements the Spring 2026 snapshot of existing coverage.
Full fibre could reach 28.1 million UK homes if all plans are realised.
The projected full-fibre share is 92% of residential properties.
The January 2026 full-fibre baseline was 24.9 million homes.
The January 2026 full-fibre baseline share was 82%.
Gigabit-capable coverage could reach 29.0 million homes.
The projected gigabit-capable share is 95%.
The January 2026 gigabit baseline was 27.1 million homes.
The January 2026 gigabit baseline share was 89%.
Projected January 2028 full-fibre coverage was revised to 90% from 95% reported previously.
High-confidence full-fibre plans could reach 87% by January 2028.
High-confidence full-fibre plans could reach 88% by January 2029.
Urban gigabit-capable coverage could increase from 24.2 million homes to 25.3 million homes.
Urban gigabit-capable coverage could increase from 93% to 97%.
Rural gigabit-capable coverage could increase from 2.9 million homes to 3.7 million homes.
Rural gigabit-capable coverage could increase from 66% to 86%.
Ofcom estimates 95% of local authorities could reach at least 85% residential gigabit coverage by January 2029.
Around 6,950 additional or upgraded geographically distinct FWA masts are planned between January 2026 and January 2029.
